newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Buyers boost Belgian bonds, but future uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Buyers boost Belgian bonds, but future uncertain.

text.p: Active bidding pushed longer maturity Belgian linear bonds higher on Tuesday, although traders said the reason for the interest after Monday's holiday was unclear as was the market's immediate future direction.
"It is very strong but also very quiet," one trader said. "There are big buyers in 10-year and longer paper, but there does not appear to be any clear reason."
However, shorter maturities, strongly bid last week, were largely neglected on Tuesday as money market rates eased back slightly after rising steeply in recent weeks, traders said.

Traders said the strength in the medium to long term maturities was not linked to either Monday's French budget audit or expectations surrounding the speech later on Tuesday by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

"We look very strong at the moment and could go even higher from here, although the (bond) auction next Monday could be a cause for some consolidation or even a slight downwards correction," one trader said.
Traders said some of Tuesday's interest had been due to interest rate swaps and involved both foreign and domestic players.
The benchmark 10-year OLO BE286= ended Tuesday yielding 5.61 percent, down from Friday's 5.65 percent, but the spread over German Bunds MEUR was barely changed at eight basis points against nine.
The front-month futures contract BGBc1 was 17 basis points higher at 122.26.
